title: KRAFTON Confirms BGMI Lite for India With End-of-2026 Launch Window
excerpt: Battlegrounds Mobile India Lite is officially happening, KRAFTON announces alongside global PUBG Mobile LIGHT reveal at World Cup 2026.
body:
• KRAFTON India confirmed on August 16 that Battlegrounds Mobile India Lite will launch in India by end of 2026, ending months of speculation.
  • The announcement came alongside the global reveal of PUBG Mobile LIGHT at the PUBG Mobile World Cup 2026, with pre-registration starting August 25.
  • BGMI Lite's exact release date, pre-registration timeline, download size, and device requirements remain unannounced.
  • BGMI has crossed 260 million downloads in India, and the Lite version aims to expand access to budget smartphone users.

KRAFTON India has officially confirmed that Battlegrounds Mobile India Lite is coming to India, with a launch targeted for the end of 2026. The announcement, made on August 16, puts an end to over seven months of speculation that began with an in-game survey in January.

"You Asked. We Listened. BGMI LITE Coming Soon."

— KRAFTON India, official BGMI announcement

The confirmation arrived on the final day of the PUBG Mobile World Cup 2026, where PUBG Mobile Producer Rick Li unveiled PUBG Mobile LIGHT — a global lighter version of the flagship battle royale. KRAFTON India followed with its own India-specific announcement confirming the domestic variant.

What KRAFTON Has Revealed So Far

Details remain deliberately sparse. KRAFTON said BGMI Lite represents "the next chapter in the evolution of the Battlegrounds Mobile India experience" and is designed to make the game accessible to a wider community of Indian players. Beyond the end-of-2026 launch window, the company has not disclosed the exact release date, pre-registration schedule, download size, system requirements, or gameplay features.

No official BGMI Lite pre-registration link exists yet. Players should avoid websites or social media posts claiming to offer early access or APK files — these remain unofficial and potentially harmful.

The Global PUBG Mobile LIGHT Connection

The global PUBG Mobile LIGHT version, announced by Rick Li, provides some indication of what a lighter PUBG experience could look like. LIGHT will require around 1GB on Android and under 2GB on iOS for its initial download, with no mandatory extra packages before the first match. It retains the Classic Erangel map, core combat mechanics, and supports cross-version play — meaning LIGHT players can team up with those using the standard PUBG Mobile app.

Existing PUBG Mobile accounts and owned items will carry over to LIGHT, and the developers plan to keep both versions updated in sync. Pre-registration for the global version begins August 25, 2026.

However, KRAFTON India's announcement does not confirm that BGMI Lite will mirror these exact specifications. The August 25 pre-registration date applies to PUBG Mobile LIGHT globally, not necessarily to BGMI Lite in India.

From Survey to Confirmation

The road to this announcement started on January 23, 2026, when KRAFTON India rolled out a detailed in-game survey. Unlike routine feedback polls, this one directly asked players: "Do you want BGMI Lite?" It went further, probing specific potential features including 20-player matches on smaller maps, fast reload mechanics without attachments, auto-aim and auto-fire options, and special weapon powers.

The survey also explored monetization preferences, asking whether players would watch ads for free gameplay or pay a monthly subscription to remove them. That level of specificity excited the community but remained market research rather than a product commitment — until now.

As recently as March 2026, industry analysts at TalkEsport assessed that a 2026 launch was unlikely, estimating that development, optimization for devices with 1-2GB RAM, and a separate regulatory approval process through Indian government agencies would push the timeline to 2027 at the earliest. KRAFTON's August 16 confirmation suggests the company moved faster than those projections anticipated.

Why It Matters for Indian Gamers

India's mobile gaming market is dominated by budget Android devices. When PUBG Mobile and PUBG Mobile Lite were banned in September 2020, millions of low-end device users lost access to the lighter variant. BGMI launched in 2021 as the Indian counterpart of PUBG Mobile, but its growing download size — now exceeding 800MB with additional resource packages — has continued to push budget device users to the margins.

With BGMI crossing 260 million downloads, a Lite version could tap into the substantial segment of players who have been unable to run the full game. The original PUBG Mobile Lite had built a massive community in India before the ban, and that demand has never gone away — it has only intensified as each BGMI update added more storage and processing requirements.

For the Indian diaspora and NRI gaming community, BGMI's Lite version could also re-engage players who grew up with PUBG Mobile Lite in India and have followed the franchise's regulatory journey from abroad.

What Comes Next

KRAFTON has indicated that more details about BGMI Lite's gameplay, features, download size, and supported devices will be announced closer to launch. Players should rely only on official KRAFTON India channels for updates and avoid third-party download links or registration forms circulating on social media.

The end-of-2026 window leaves room for a Q4 release, potentially aligning with the festive season when mobile gaming activity in India typically peaks. Whether BGMI Lite will launch simultaneously with or after the global PUBG Mobile LIGHT rollout remains to be seen.
